title: one notes table with a tenant policy, read as six different roles

steps.note: a notes table owned by an ordinary role, rows for two tenants, and a policy: you see your tenant's rows, named by app.tenant.
the clerk, working for acme. no WHERE in the query; the policy adds one.
the same clerk, same query, working for globex.
the clerk with no tenant set: current_setting returns NULL, the policy is never true, and the clerk sees nothing.
the acme clerk tries to write a note for globex. with only USING, the policy's expression is also the check for new rows, and this row fails it.

error.message: new row violates row-level security policy for table "notes"

steps.note: the table's owner: policies don't apply to the owner, so it sees every row.
FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY makes the owner subject to the policy too.
a role created with BYPASSRLS ignores policies, even forced ones.

steps.sql:
RESET ROLE;
SELECT id, tenant, body FROM notes ORDER BY id
steps.note: and a superuser (postgres, who set all this up) always bypasses them.
